You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: claude-opus-5-5.
Game: art of rally.
About the game: A top-down rally driving game. The run opens at the beginning of a custom rally. Driving stages alternate with result and continuation screens, ending at the final rally result.
Controls:
W is throttle, S is brake/reverse, A and D steer left and right, and Space is the handbrake. Enter confirms the displayed menu or result selection. The car uses automatic transmission. The driving-only preparation disables in-race pause, manual recovery and restart; automatic recovery and result navigation remain available.
Choose one ordinary keyboard input to hold for one second. Each option specifies the key or keys held together.
Group controls: W is throttle, S is brake/reverse, A and D steer, Space is the handbrake, and Enter confirms a displayed menu or result selection.
  throttle: Hold W: throttle.
  throttle_left: Hold W and A: throttle and left steering.
  throttle_right: Hold W and D: throttle and right steering.
  brake_reverse: Hold S: brake or reverse.
  brake_reverse_left: Hold S and A: brake or reverse with left steering.
  brake_reverse_right: Hold S and D: brake or reverse with right steering.
  steer_left: Hold A: left steering without throttle or brake.
  steer_right: Hold D: right steering without throttle or brake.
  handbrake: Hold Space: handbrake.
  handbrake_left: Hold Space and A: handbrake and left steering.
  handbrake_right: Hold Space and D: handbrake and right steering.
  throttle_handbrake: Hold W and Space: throttle and handbrake.
  throttle_handbrake_left: Hold W, Space and A: throttle, handbrake and left steering.
  throttle_handbrake_right: Hold W, Space and D: throttle, handbrake and right steering.
  confirm: Hold Enter: confirm the displayed menu or result selection.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game is paused while you think, then each action uses a nominal 1 s host-time step. Input is released before any integration-specific rendering wait, then the game pauses again. Native simulation time depends on speed, native pause and performance. Rendering waits consume the same wall-clock budget. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.

answers.hardest_part: Hitting all 19 checkpoints per stage while maintaining speed and staying on-road. The 1-second discrete input window makes precise steering difficult on tight corners, and I'll need to anticipate turns and chain handbrake inputs correctly to navigate sharp curves without missing checkpoint gates.
answers.likely_failure: Missing checkpoints on tight corners by either going off-road, cutting the corner too much to miss the gate, or undershooting the turn and losing trajectory. Secondary failure mode: running out of time on later stages if I'm too conservative early on, or crashing on a particularly sharp section.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Automatic transmission eliminates a decision layer; handbrake provides tight directional control critical for rally; game auto-saves progress so stage completion accumulates points even if I fail later; top-down view clearly shows the road layout and upcoming turns.
answers.harmful_mechanics: 1-second input discretization makes fine steering adjustments difficult; no pause/restart capability means one major mistake can cascade; no manual recovery from off-road; depth perception in top-down view makes it harder to judge precise car positioning relative to checkpoint gates; learning curve with unfamiliar car physics within time pressure.
